cover.title: Johnny × Zach Harris — Tribe.ai Referral Brief
cover.subtitle: Pre-loop intelligence call. Aperture expanded (FDE → FDPM title unlocked). Coaching received but recoil zone demonstrated live in the same call. NCI: 78 — strong referral signal, behavioral flag confirmed once. One pattern to suppress before Friday.
cover.meta: ARCS RECOIL · Jun 23, 2026 · ~47 min call · 7 segments · Reverse Listening + Deep Recall

loadBearingQuote.text: Read the room carefully. Not everyone you meet is going to be so heady.
loadBearingQuote.attribution: Johnny, ~75% mark — delivered after Zach demoed Observatory and Recoil Report mid-coaching call, demonstrating the exact behavior being warned about

callWalk.label: Seg 1 · 0–15%
callWalk.title: Rapport Baseline — LA / NYC / Kids
callWalk.body: Extended geography and family rapport (5+ min) before any role content. Warm and genuine — this is a friendship call with a business purpose embedded in it. The length signals real relationship depth, which is the referral's actual value.

callWalk.label: Seg 2 · 15–29%
callWalk.title: APERTURE UNLOCK — FDE → FDPM Title
callWalk.body: Johnny reframes the talent landscape: AI native services as the #1 opportunity, forward deployed PM as a distinct role Zach hadn't been searching for. Zach: 'I didn't even consider looking for forward deployed PM roles.' Prior corrected live. This is the most durable information gain of the call.

callWalk.label: Seg 3 · 29–43%
callWalk.title: Pod Structure + Client Reality
callWalk.body: Prudential detail (1,600 APIs, Jenkins → GitHub Actions, 6-month compression of 16-month timeline). Flat org, high agency, no tooling dictates, one dedicated client per FDE. 'We've already met our revenue number for the year.' All confirmed later by Mariana and Julia — Johnny's Intel was accurate.

callWalk.label: Seg 4 · 43–57%
callWalk.title: Interview Loop Mapped in Full
callWalk.body: 3-module Loom take-home: (1) mindset/approach, (2) drop-in scenario / next-2-weeks sprint, (3) build a triage system end-to-end. Co-founder meeting: personal questions, not career. Hot take is asked at every stage. Speed compression via competing-offer disclosure confirmed. BEHAVIORAL FLAG: Zach asks 'Are they looking for variance in the hot take?' — meta-gaming the process rather than just having one ready. Johnny: 'I don't think it matters at all.'

callWalk.label: Seg 5 · 57–71%
callWalk.title: RECOIL ZONE — Live Demonstration
callWalk.body: Zach shares his hot take (knowledge economy convergence), then drops the Observatory link and pitches the Recoil Report as a potential internal tool. Johnny's response is polite-but-pivoting. This is the same behavior the warning at Seg 7 addresses — but the warning comes AFTER this segment, meaning Johnny observed the behavior before articulating the risk.

callWalk.label: Seg 6 · 71–86%
callWalk.title: Strategic Drift — Acqui-hire, PE, M&A
callWalk.body: Zach pivots toward macro ecosystem questions (acquisition play, hedge fund clients, M&A synergies). Johnny deflects each one: 'They are founder-led, not trying to flip.' Pattern: Zach gravitates toward macro/ecosystem framing (comfort zone) while Johnny keeps trying to ground the conversation in practical interview prep.

callWalk.label: Seg 7 · 86–100%
callWalk.title: Warning Delivered + Warm Close
callWalk.body: Johnny: 'Read the room carefully. Not everyone you meet is going to be so heady.' IP assignment note. 'You should thank yourself.' This is the most load-bearing moment — not because it's harsh, but because it's the only thing Johnny said that required active correction of Zach's behavior rather than additional coaching.

signalThreads.label: Referral Quality
signalThreads.title: Genuine enthusiasm — not transactional
signalThreads.body: Johnny is recommending 5 people across multiple roles. His Intel was accurate across all three data points later verified (pod structure, client reality, interview loop). He stayed on for ~47 min of detailed coaching. This is a warm referral in the strong sense.

signalThreads.label: Recoil Zone 1
signalThreads.title: Altitude mismatch demonstrated live
signalThreads.body: Zach demoed Observatory and Recoil Report mid-Intel-briefing, while Johnny was trying to map the interview loop. The behavior was self-reinforcing: each new product idea extended the call past the practical coaching agenda. Johnny warned about it precisely because he had just watched it happen.
signalThreads.note: Confirmed once. Must not appear in Mariana or Julia calls.

signalThreads.label: Recoil Zone 2
signalThreads.title: Meta-gaming the process
signalThreads.body: Asking whether 'variance in the hot take matters across people' signals analysis of the interview structure rather than authentic preparation. Johnny's answer was definitive: the question doesn't have a strategic answer. Have a take, say it.

signalThreads.label: Recovery
signalThreads.title: Aperture correction was immediate
signalThreads.body: Zach updated his search framing live on the call (FDE → FDPM). Acknowledged the coaching. Committed to flagging competing processes. The corrective instinct is intact — the problem is execution lag between receiving a signal and adjusting.

best.title: Referral converts to fast-tracked loop
best.body: Johnny's coaching on urgency lever is used immediately with Mariana. Loop compresses to 1–2 weeks. Behavioral correction holds across all remaining calls — no altitude mismatch with any interviewer.
best.note: Requires: mentioning competing processes to Mariana on Friday, not over-demoing product during interview stages.

base.title: Standard loop — 3–4 weeks
base.body: Referral smooths entry. Interview proceeds at normal pace. Take-home is strong. Co-founder meeting lands on personal register. Offer comes.
base.note: Most likely path if urgency lever lands but altitude issue persists in one interview without derailing.

worst.title: Altitude mismatch kills the take-home stage
worst.body: The 3-module Loom requires demonstrating product thinking clearly on screen. If Zach goes heady in the take-home commentary (too much ARCS philosophy, not enough clear delivery artifacts), the hiring team can't read the capability. The signal is there but doesn't project.
worst.note: Mitigation: treat take-home modules as executive-altitude deliverables, not exploratory design sessions.

riskFlags.label: Behavioral Pattern — Altitude
riskFlags.body: Demonstrated live during a coaching call with someone who has known Zach for years and forgives it. Mariana and the co-founder interview will not have that buffer. The fix is mechanical: answer at executive altitude first, offer depth on request.

riskFlags.label: Meta-gaming tendency
riskFlags.body: Asking 'are they looking for variance in the hot take' is a tell. It signals optimizing for the game rather than playing it. Tribe explicitly tests for authentic AI takes — the only right answer is a real one.

riskFlags.label: Intel accuracy
riskFlags.body: Johnny's briefing was accurate across every claim later verified. Trust the loop structure he mapped. Don't over-prepare for things he didn't flag.

riskFlags.label: Referral signal is strong
riskFlags.body: Five referrals placed, none rejected outright yet. Johnny is vouching hard. The path is clear — the only variable is behavioral execution, not qualification or fit.

protocol.label: Fix 01
protocol.title: Urgency lever — activate on first recruiter call
protocol.body: Mention competing processes. Let Mariana offer to compress. Do not volunteer enthusiasm ranking ('most fun opportunity') — it removes leverage before it's been earned.

protocol.label: Fix 02
protocol.title: Suppress demo instinct during interview stages
protocol.body: Observatory, Recoil Report, and ARCS architecture are proof-of-build only when asked for. The right ask: 'Would you like me to drop a link?' Not a pre-emptive share.

protocol.label: Fix 03
protocol.title: Have the hot take ready — one sentence
protocol.body: Johnny's take: 'It's infrastructure like anything else.' Zach's is the knowledge/sharing economy convergence. Commit to one, say it cleanly, stop. No exploration mid-answer.

protocol.label: Prep 04
protocol.title: Loom take-home: build deliverables, not documents
protocol.body: Module 3 requires a triage system with artifacts. Lead with the artifact. Walk the logic after. Tone: product demo, not design essay.
